title: plugin-hono-server compression: a 304 with no Content-Type gets no Vary: Accept-Encoding, while the README and docs say every 304 does
body:
domain:server#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaAUev5V62cLHhQwBi

Filing category: ② docs-versus-behaviour gap, low (escalated by the TIER_DEFAULT review of PR #32491 for #32155, comment 6815452954 ③; read from the code, not run).
Refs #32155 · Refs #32491

## Business reason

The self-hosted server's response compression (PR #32491) adds `Vary: Accept-Encoding` so caches keep compressed and uncompressed copies apart. The README, `http-protocol.mdx` and the changeset say `304` answers carry that `Vary` too. For the `304` answers the platform actually sends, they do not, so the docs promise more than the server does. No cache result is wrong today, because a cache refreshing a stored answer from a `304` keeps the stored `Vary`.

## What happens

1. The middleware decides whether a response is of an encodable kind from its `Content-Type`. It appends `Vary` for every such response, including `HEAD`, `206` and `304` after the Y′ patch round.
2. A `304` usually carries no `Content-Type`, so the rule cannot tell what its `200` would have carried, and no `Vary` is added.
3. Both `304` producers in the tree have that shape: `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` (the stable-file branch) and `packages/runtime/src/domains/i18n.ts`.

## Expected

Either the docs say exactly what the server does (a `304` carries `Vary: Accept-Encoding` only when it carries a compressible `Content-Type`), or the middleware adds `Vary` to a `304` whose route would encode its `200`. Then pin it with a `304` case in `response-compression.test.ts`.

Re-check (premise): after #32491 lands, read the `Vary` branch of `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/response-compression.ts` and the two `304` producers above.
Reader who acts: the seat that owns `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server`.
